target.title: fix(auto-reply): self-heal reply-session-init conflict instead of permanently wedging the session
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the reply-session initializer's optimistic-concurrency commit (`commitReplySessionInitialization`) loses its race twice, the current code throws `"reply session initialization conflicted"` and permanently wedges the session. Because the store entry is never committed, every subsequent turn on the same `sessionKey` re-hits the identical conflict — completed tool-results silently return empty, and the session only recovers with a manual `/reset` or fresh session.

Fixes [#102020](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/102020). Also addresses the root cause of [#101909](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101909).

## Why This Change Was Made

The conflict branch in `initSessionStateAttemptLocked` allowed exactly one stale-snapshot retry and then threw. The rollover/timeout paths already self-heal by disposing the session's MCP runtime and running the registered harness `reset` hooks. This change makes the conflict branch reuse that same recovery once and retry initialization before giving up.

### Conflict resolution state machine

| State | staleSnapshotRetried | conflictRecoveryAttempted | Action |
|-------|---------------------|--------------------------|--------|
| First | false | any | stale-snapshot-retry (unchanged) |
| Second | true | false | **self-heal-retry** — dispose wedged MCP runtime + harness reset, then retry (new) |
| Third | true | true | fail — throw with clear context |

### Safety fence

The self-heal reuses the same `runExclusiveSessionLifecycleMutation` + `interruptSessionWorkAdmissions` fence the rollover path uses: drains any foreign in-flight turn OUTSIDE the store-write lock before tearing anything down.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Second message → "reply session initialization conflicted" → permanently wedged → every subsequent message silently dropped → only `/reset` recovers
- **After**: Self-heal disposes wedged runtime + retries → init completes → session recovers automatically → reply delivered normally

## Evidence

### 1. E2E: Same-session conflict → self-heal → reply delivered (NOT dropped/empty)

`src/auto-reply/reply/e2e-conflict-recovery.test.ts` simulates the exact #102020 scenario: message 1 works, Codex harness changes session identity between turns, message 2 hits repeated CAS conflicts, self-heal recovers, reply is delivered:

```
$ pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/e2e-conflict-recovery.test.ts -- --reporter verbose

═══ MESSAGE 1: first message in fresh session ═══
  SessionKey: agent:main:dashboard:e2e-conflict-user

    [CAS commit #1] ACCEPTED — revision matches, store committed
  ✓ Message 1: sessionId=3cc09c0f-...
  ✓ Message 1: reply delivered normally (no error)

═══ BETWEEN TURNS: concurrent activity ═══
  Codex harness writes transcript mirror...
  → sessionFile field changed in store

═══ MESSAGE 2: second message in same session ═══

    [CAS commit #2] REJECTED — revision mismatch (4 forced remaining)
    [CAS commit #3] REJECTED — revision mismatch (3 forced remaining)
          ↑ self-heal triggers: dispose wedged MCP runtime + harness reset
    [CAS commit #4] REJECTED — revision mismatch (2 forced remaining)
    [CAS commit #5] REJECTED — revision mismatch (1 forced remaining)
          ↑ fenced revalidation: drain + teardown + retry
    [CAS commit #6] ACCEPTED — revision matches, store committed

═══ VERIFICATION ═══
  ✓ Same sessionKey: agent:main:dashboard:e2e-conflict-user
  ✓ Message 1 sessionId: 3cc09c0f-...
  ✓ Message 2 sessionId: 3cc09c0f-...
  ✓ Both messages processed in same session: true
  ✓ CAS commit attempts: 6 (#1=msg1 OK, #2-5=rejected, #6=self-heal OK)
  ✓ Message 2 reply DELIVERED (not empty/dropped)
  ✓ Wedged runtime disposed: true

  RESULT: Same session delivered 2 messages
  Message 1 → OK | Conflict → Self-heal → Message 2 → OK
  Zero dropped replies, zero empty tool results

 ✓ 1 passed (541ms)
```

### 2. Gateway runtime: patched agent processes real messages end-to-end

```
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local \
    --session-key "agent:main:dashboard:gw-verify-final" \
    --message "Say hello in one short sentence"

[trace:embedded-run] startup stages:
  sessionId=206d6aa5-...  totalMs=18505

[trace:embedded-run] prep stages:
  agent-session:61ms     ← initSessionState with self-heal code

[model-fetch] start provider=zte model=Qwen3-235B-A22B
[model-fetch] response status=200 elapsedMs=2448

Hello! 👋

[agent] run ended with stopReason=stop
```

Session init completed, model responded, reply delivered, clean stop. No crash, no "reply session initialization conflicted".

### 3. Unit tests for conflict decision helper

```
$ pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.test.ts
✓ retries with fresh snapshot on first conflict
✓ self-heals instead of throwing once stale-snapshot retry is exhausted
✓ only self-heals once, then fails clearly
✓ prefers stale-snapshot retry even after recovery ran
Test Files  1 passed (1) | Tests  4 passed (4)
```

### 4. Full regression suite (219 tests, zero regressions)

```
Test Files  7 passed (7) | Tests  219 passed (219)
```

## Changes

- `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.ts` (new): `resolveReplyInitConflictAction()` — 3-action state machine
- `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.test.ts` (new): 4 unit tests
- `src/auto-reply/reply/session-init-self-heal.test.ts` (new): 2 integration tests forcing CAS conflicts
- `src/auto-reply/reply/self-heal-visible-demo.test.ts` (new): step-by-step console output
- `src/auto-reply/reply/e2e-conflict-recovery.test.ts` (new): same-session 2-message E2E proof
- `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts`: adds `conflict-self-heal` outcome type + `selfHealReplySessionInitConflict()` + 3-action conflict resolution
